clue.text: Party material that's right for the Cabinet

parts.note: chiffon is a sheer fabric favoured for party dresses
i.e. (id est) means 'that is'

explanation.surface: A host chooses suitable fabric with which to drape the cabinet before a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's' is expanded to 'that is', the gloss of the Latin abbreviation i.e.
explanation.definitionFit: A chiffonier is a tall chest of drawers or sideboard, a kind of cabinet furniture.

clue.text: Navigator brought back some tobacco

indicators.note: brought back means that portion is read from right to left
some means only part of the word tobacco is taken

explanation.surface: A sailor returned with a supply of tobacco from the New World.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking some of 'tobacco' gives TOBAC; 'brought back' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: John Cabot was the Italian-born explorer who sailed for England to North America in 1497.

clue.text: Gogol made play with this general

definitions.text: Gogol made play with this general

parts.words: Gogol made play with this general
parts.note: Gogol's comic play is known in English as The Government ... or as the title with general appended

explanation.definitionFit: The Inspector General is the English title of Gogol's satirical comedy about an official taken for a government auditor.

clue.text: Predictably they can be made to return toll fees

indicators.note: can be made says the letters of the three words may be formed into something else

explanation.surface: Booths collecting tolls are told to refund the fees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be made' rearranges RETURNTOLLFEES; 'Predictably they' is the definition, punning on prediction.
explanation.definitionFit: Clairvoyants make predictions, so they are the people who predict.

clue.text: Fresh purchase about right in town of course

parts.note: fresh means new

indicators.note: about means the word for purchase surrounds the letter for right

parts.note: a purchase is something you buy

explanation.surface: A new buy in a town, naturally, is just right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of course' reads as 'naturally' but means 'with a racecourse': Newbury, Berkshire, is a racing town.
explanation.definitionFit: Newbury is a Berkshire town known for its racecourse, home to major horse races.

clue.text: See 15

annotationWithheld.why: Clue is 'See 15' (7): it has no wordplay of its own; ELEMENT is only the word '5' inside 15 across's definition 'a 17 5', so nothing in the clues builds it.

clue.text: Snap report?

definitions.meaning: a snap is a quick photograph, a snapshot
a report is the bang of a gun being fired

explanation.definitionFit: A photograph is a shot, and so is the firing of a gun, which gives a report.

clue.text: An engaging fellow

parts.note: read as charming, but means a man who engages, that is takes on, staff or goods for pay

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who rents or employs is one who engages people or things.

clue.text: Commercial chaps who "have … their entrances"

parts.note: echoes Shakespeare's 'They have their exits and their entrances', while houses have side doors for delivery men

explanation.definitionFit: Shopkeepers and delivery men use the side door named for them in large houses.

clue.text: Survivalists buoyant ? They're loaded !

definitions.meaning: buoyant devices keeping people afloat to survive in water
short clubs weighted with lead, used as coshes

explanation.definitionFit: Lifebelts and jackets keep people afloat, and the same name is given to weighted coshes carried for defence.

clue.text: Pick the plant of sorrow, say-so to cover the ground

parts.note: the pick of the bunch is the best

indicators.note: say signals that the word for the herb is only spoken, then spelt differently

parts.note: rue is the herb of grace and of sorrow, its name meaning regret

explanation.surface: A mourner chooses the herb of regret to scatter over a grave.
explanation.walkthrough: Rue is traditionally the plant of sorrow (Ophelia's herb); 'say' gives its sound respelt as the old word REW.
explanation.definitionFit: To bestrew is to scatter things over a surface, strewing them across the floor.

clue.text: Retire perhaps to a province in' Africa

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters of the word Retire might be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Someone thinks of retiring to a territory on the African continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' is the anagram signal on 'Retire'. When this was set, Eritrea was still a province of Ethiopia.
explanation.definitionFit: Eritrea, on the Red Sea coast, was then administered as an Ethiopian province before its independence in 1993.

clue.text: Something for 3 to look into

parts.note: 3 down are clairvoyants who peer into crystal balls, and what they claim to see is what lies ahead

explanation.definitionFit: Fortune tellers claim to foresee coming events, which is what lies ahead in time.

clue.text: Was Eastlake so strange ?

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east
Erie is one of the North American Great Lakes

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a place called Eastlake was uncanny.
explanation.walkthrough: The single word 'Eastlake' splits into 'East' and 'lake', so the lake is named and the compass point abbreviated.
explanation.definitionFit: Eerie means weird and unsettling, a synonym for strange.

clue.text: The joint — topside for Dr Proudic

definitions.meaning: a carpentry joint cut at an angle, as in a picture frame corner
Dr Proudie is the bishop in Trollope's Barchester novels, and his headgear is a tall pointed hat

explanation.surface: A carver offers a joint of beef, topside, to a guest named Dr Proudie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joint' and 'topside' suggest cuts of beef; topside is really the bishop's head covering.
explanation.definitionFit: A mitre is both an angled woodworking joint and the headdress worn by a bishop.

clue.text: "Astley, and Sir ——, and Rupert of the Rhine" (Macaulay)

definitions.text: "Astley, and Sir ——, and Rupert of the Rhine" (Macaulay)

parts.words: "Astley, and Sir ——, and Rupert of the Rhine" (Macaulay)
parts.note: a line from Macaulay's The Battle of Naseby naming Royalist commanders

explanation.definitionFit: Sir Marmaduke Langdale was a Royalist cavalry commander at Naseby, named in Macaulay's poem.

clue.text: Betty Muir can make a 17 5

indicators.note: can make says the letters of the two names may be formed into something new

explanation.surface: A woman called Betty Muir is able to produce a rare substance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can make' signals rearranging BETTYMUIR; the definition refers to 17 across and 5 down together.
explanation.definitionFit: Ytterbium is one of the lanthanides, the metals known as rare earth elements.

clue.text: China, or tension, broken

indicators.note: broken suggests the letters of the two words are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: Fine porcelain, or strain in the household, ends up shattered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges ORTENSION. 'China' is pottery, not the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Ironstone is a hard, durable kind of earthenware, sold as ironstone china.

clue.text: Not common-or-garden soil

parts.note: read as an uncommon kind of dirt, but means a class of scarce metallic oxides

explanation.definitionFit: Rare earths are oxides of the lanthanide metals, so-called though not soil at all.

clue.text: Down-to earth sort of string to pull

definitions.text: Down-to earth sort of string to pull

parts.words: Down-to earth sort of string to pull
parts.note: read as a practical string to pull, but means the cord a parachutist tugs to float down to the ground

explanation.definitionFit: A parachutist pulls this cord to open the canopy and descend to the ground.

clue.text: Odd Nazi greeting to the State going the rounds

indicators.note: odd signals that the greeting's letters are set out in an unusual order

parts.note: Heil was the Nazi salute
Cal is a short form of California, a US state

explanation.surface: A strange Nazi salute is given to the state as it circulates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd' is the anagram signal on the greeting; 'going the rounds' means circling, not making social calls.
explanation.definitionFit: Helical describes a spiral or coil, something winding round and round.

clue.text: One eloping with a dish?

parts.note: the nursery rhyme Hey Diddle Diddle ends with the dish running away with a piece of cutlery

explanation.definitionFit: In the rhyme, the dish ran away with this piece of cutlery.

clue.text: England's on the ——, hear the hammers ring

definitions.text: England's on the ——, hear the hammers ring

parts.words: England's on the ——, hear the hammers ring
parts.note: a line from Kipling's poem The ..., where the missing word is the smith's iron block

explanation.definitionFit: A blacksmith's heavy iron block, struck by hammers, completes Kipling's line.

clue.text: See The Ring on this tape?

parts.note: vide is Latin for see, used in references
O is the shape of a ring

explanation.surface: Someone suggests watching a Wagner opera recording on a cassette.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Ring' looks like Wagner's opera cycle; it is only the shape of O.
explanation.definitionFit: Videotape is the magnetic tape used to record moving pictures.

clue.text: Gave arbitrary direction to a sub editor

parts.note: Polaris was the class of nuclear missile submarine, so Polaris names a sub

explanation.surface: Someone assigns a submarine's editor a random course.
explanation.walkthrough: Polaris was the missile carried by Britain's 1960s nuclear submarines, which took its name.
explanation.definitionFit: To polarise is to give a fixed orientation to light or magnetism, imposing an axis.

clue.text: Doctor mainly behind with banker's order

parts.note: aft means behind on a ship, so on the main (the sea)

explanation.surface: A physician mostly trails behind with a bank instruction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mainly' is not 'mostly' but 'on the main' (the high seas), where aft is the word for behind.
explanation.definitionFit: A draft is a written order from a bank to pay a sum, like a banker's cheque.

clue.text: Rare way to cook Cerberus without his tail ?

indicators.note: without his tail means the final letter of the dog's description is dropped

parts.note: Cerberus guards the underworld, so he is a dog from under the earth

explanation.surface: Someone wonders how to cook the hound of Hades rare once his tail is gone.
explanation.walkthrough: Cerberus, the three-headed hound guarding Hades, is punningly an 'under dog': a dog of the world below.
explanation.definitionFit: To underdo meat is to cook it lightly so it stays rare in the middle.

clue.text: Give credit note to girl for this violin

parts.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit
E is one of the musical notes
Mona is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A suitor credits a young woman with a note for a fine fiddle.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cremona is a violin made in Cremona, home of Stradivari and Amati.

clue.text: Blackwood's poetic form ?

parts.note: reads as verse in Blackwood's Magazine, but means the poetic word for black timber

explanation.definitionFit: Ebon is the literary, poetic version of ebony, a black wood.

clue.text: Perhaps a second late, otherwise pre-mature

indicators.note: otherwise signals that the letters of the two words are put in a different order

explanation.surface: Someone a moment late is, by a twisted reading, premature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'otherwise' rearranges SECONDLATE; 'Perhaps a' links. The hyphen in 'pre-mature' gives the sense of not yet fully adult.
explanation.definitionFit: A teenager is not yet mature, still in the years before adulthood.
